## Overview

This tutorial walks through the full XCMS-only pipeline from raw mzXML/mzML
files to a processed feature table. This step is optional: start here only
if you have raw files. Its feature table is the input for vignette 2a.

The pipeline uses five step functions, or `runxcmsFT()` to run them all:

```{r overview-table, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
df <- data.frame(
  Step     = 0:5,
  Function = c(
    "runXCMSProcessing()",
    "getChromPeaks()",
    "linkCPtoFeatures()",
    "buildFeatureTable()",
    "processFeatureTable()",
    "runxcmsFT()"
  ),
  Output = c(
    "XcmsExperiment + sample metadata",
    "Raw chromPeaks data.frame",
    "chromPeaks + feature_id column",
    "Feature defs + intensity matrix",
    "Sorted, feature_name, intensity_median, intensity_mean",
    "Steps 0-4 in one call"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

if (requireNamespace("kableExtra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  kableExtra::kable(df, align = c("c", "l", "l")) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width        = FALSE,
      position          = "left"
    ) |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, width = "3em") |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(2,width = "10em", monospace = TRUE, color = "black") |> #"#2166ac"
    kableExtra::row_spec(6, bold = TRUE, background = "#f0f7ff")
} else {
  knitr::kable(df, align = c("c", "l", "l"))
}
```

---

## 1 Load packages

```{r packages}
library(MS1Match)
library(xcms)

library(MsExperiment)
library(BiocParallel)
library(S4Vectors)
```

---

## 2 Set XCMS parameters

Parameters are defined as standard xcms `Param` objects and passed into the
pipeline. All three are optional -- if omitted, the pipeline falls back to
built-in defaults tuned for Bruker maXis HD / UHPLC / positive ESI.

### 2.1 Peak picking - CentWave

```{r centwave-params}
cwp <- CentWaveParam(
  peakwidth          = c(5, 20),   
  ppm                = 5,          
  snthresh           = 10,         
  mzdiff             = 0.001,      
  prefilter          = c(3, 1000), 
  noise              = 500,        
  verboseBetaColumns = TRUE        # retains beta_cor / beta_snr in chromPeaks
)
```

> **Note:** For detailed guidance on parameter selection, please refer to the
> [xcms documentation](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/xcms.html)
> and the `?CentWaveParam` help page.


### 2.2 Feature grouping - PeakDensity

```{r peakdensity-params}
pdp <- PeakDensityParam(
  sampleGroups = c("3ul"),
  bw           = 5,     
  minFraction  = 0.5,   
  binSize      = 0.01  
)
```

### 2.3 RT alignment - Obiwarp

```{r obiwarp-params}
obi <- ObiwarpParam(binSize = 0.5)

```

---

## 3 Run the full pipeline

### 3.1 Pipeline function

`runxcmsFT()` runs all five steps and returns a named list.

```{r run-pipeline}
xcms_out <- runxcmsFT(
  files_dir    = system.file("extdata", "mix84_data", package = "MS1Match"), 
  cwp          = cwp,
  pdp          = pdp,
  obi          = obi,
  sample_name  = c("3ul"),
  sample_group = c("3ul"),
  BPPARAM      = SnowParam(workers = 4)   
)
```

Retrieve xcms_outputs:

```{r extract-xcms_outputs}
xcms_output_result <- xcms_out$result     # list(x_exp, pd)
xcms_output_cp     <- xcms_out$cp         # all detected chromPeaks
xcms_output_cpft   <- xcms_out$cp_linked  # chromPeaks with feature_id
xcms_output_ft     <- xcms_out$ft         # final processed feature table
```







### 3.2 Step-by-step approach

Users can inspect or modify intermediate objects.

```{r step-by-step, eval=FALSE}
# Step 0 -- XCMS processing
result <- runXCMSProcessing(
  files_dir    = "yourdata/mzXML/",
  cwp          = cwp,
  pdp          = pdp,
  obi          = obi,
  sample_name  = c("WT_1", "WT_2", "WT_3", "KO_1", "KO_2", "KO_3"),
  sample_group = c(rep("WT", 3), rep("KO", 3)),
  BPPARAM      = SnowParam(workers = 4)
)

# Step 1 -- raw chromPeaks
cp <- getChromPeaks(result$x_exp)

# Step 2 -- chromPeaks linked to feature IDs
cp_linked <- linkCPtoFeatures(result$x_exp)

# Step 3 -- feature table (feature defs + intensity matrix)
ft_raw <- buildFeatureTable(result$x_exp)

# Step 4 -- post-process: sort by RT, add feature_name + intensity_median, intensity_mean
xcms_output_ft <- processFeatureTable(ft_raw, result$x_exp)
```

---

## 4 Inspect xcms_outputs

### 4.1 chromPeaks (Step 1)

One row per detected peak across all samples.

```{r inspect-cp,eval=FALSE}
dim(cp)
head(cp)
```

Key columns: `mz`, `mzmin`, `mzmax`, `rt`, `rtmin`, `rtmax`, `into`
(integrated area), `maxo` (apex intensity), `sample`, `sample_name`.

### 4.2 chromPeaks linked to features (Step 2)

Same as above with `feature_id` appended. `NA` means the peak was not
grouped into any feature.

```{r inspect-cp-linked, eval=FALSE}
# How many peaks were assigned to a feature?
table(is.na(cp_linked$feature_id))

# Peaks for a specific feature
cp_linked[cp_linked$feature_id == "FT0001" & !is.na(cp_linked$feature_id), ]
```

### 4.3 Feature table (Step 4)

One row per feature. Columns: feature metadata, one intensity column per
sample, and `intensity_median` and `intensity_mean`.

```{r inspect-ft,eval=FALSE}
dim(xcms_output_ft)
head(xcms_output_ft[, 1:10])


summary(xcms_output_ft$intensity_median)
```

---

## 5 Export

```{r export , eval=FALSE}
exportFeatureTable(xcms_output_ft, "xcms_output_feature_table.csv")
```

---

## 6 Parameter defaults reference

If no parameters are passed, `runXCMSProcessing()` / `runxcmsFT()` use:

```{r param-table, echo=FALSE,  eval=TRUE}
params_df <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("peakwidth", "ppm", "snthresh", "mzdiff", "noise",
                "bw", "minFraction", "binSize (pdp)", "BPPARAM"),
  Default   = c("c(5, 20)", "5", "10", "0.001", "500",
                "5", "0.5", "0.01", "SerialParam()"),
  Notes     = c(
    "UHPLC; use c(10, 30) for standard HPLC",
    "maXis HD; use 10 for generic QTOF",
    "Lower to 5 if standards are missed",
    "High-res; use 0.01 for low-res",
    "Set from diagnoseParams()",
    "Increase to 10 for larger RT drift",
    "Use 0.25 for exploratory runs",
    "High-res; use 0.1 for low-res",
    "Use SnowParam(workers = 4) to parallelise"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

if (requireNamespace("kableExtra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  kableExtra::kable(params_df, align = c("l", "l", "l")) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width        = FALSE,
      position          = "left"
    ) |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(1, monospace = TRUE, bold = TRUE,  color = "#2166ac") |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(2, monospace = TRUE)
} else {
  knitr::kable(params_df, align = c("l", "l", "l"))
}
```
